confidentUnsupported.evidence: 'this tripping is usually caused by an earth leak in the power module or wiring rather than simple overload' - hedged with usually and offers an alternative, so not a definitive diagnosis

rationale: The assistant immediately issued a stop-use and referred the customer to an electrician or appliance engineer, which matches the ground-truth escalation direction and is safe given weekly recurring trips; it correctly limited DIY to a power-off visual check. However it asked no triage questions at all (which switch trips, smells, boil-over pattern), so the customer's actual evidence (faint electrical smell, boil-overs, two zones on high) was never surfaced, and it leaned toward an earth-leak-in-module explanation while downplaying the equally plausible overload/circuit cause. Telling the owner of a built-in hob to leave it 'unplugged' is also imprecise where isolating at the cooker switch is the practical step.
